title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Wayfinding System. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Wayfinding System
options.lineage: Transit and hospital wayfinding signage: line colors, station panels, platform maps
options.thesis: Your career as a transit map. Each case study is a line with its own color, and the arm-identity panel is the first sign you read, legible in one second like a platform sign.
materials: enamel sign panels (ink with white type)
options.viewport: Left: a large ink sign panel with the headline set like station signage and a cobalt route strip. Right: the live arm panel from the Surgical Console, four arms in their line colors, which visitors can switch between states. Below the fold, a line map threads the four case studies as stations.
options.risk: Reads as a theme if the map is decorative. Every line, color and stop has to mean something real (projects, years, roles).

raised.raise: Asymmetry as law: the hero splits 7/5 with the sign panel bleeding off the left edge, never centered.
Wayfinding is reading: every section sign uses its plain literal name (Case studies, Experience, Contact).
No decorative grey: sign panels are pure ink and white. Color only ever means a line or a state.
Fixed regions: on case studies the line map stays docked as a progress rail while the content changes.
Complete keyboard operation: the arm panel takes keys 1 to 4 and arrows, and the line map is tabbable stop by stop.
Measured grid: everything sits on an 8px grid, and metrics read as signboard readouts aligned to it.

options.label: Design Handoff Spec
options.lineage: Design-to-engineering handoff sheets: redlines, specs, annotated frames
options.thesis: The portfolio as a handoff document. Every page shows the work with its measurements and decisions annotated.
options.viewport: The headline selected as a frame with live measurements, an inspector panel beside it, and the arm panel as the selected component.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most UX portfolios that try to be clever land, and v2's first hero already did it.

options.label: Raku Smoke Flash
options.case: Fuses poorly: hiring managers don't read their work through a kiln.
options.kept: Asymmetry accepted as the compositional law.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.case: Fuses poorly: irony fights the honest, crisp voice.
options.kept: Every zone labeled with its literal name.

options.label: Op-Art Repeat
options.case: Fuses poorly: optical flex hurts reading case studies.
options.kept: No grey whatsoever: geometry and contrast carry everything.

options.label: PC-98 Sixteen Color
options.case: Fuses poorly: retro novelty undercuts a modern product-design pitch.
options.kept: Fixed regions that never move; navigation swaps contents.

options.label: ANSI BBS Nightboard
options.case: Fuses poorly: a terminal costume for a designer reads as engineer-only.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.case: Fuses poorly: an instrument costume, and too close to the surgical subject's own tools.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean product-designer portfolio: name and role, a grid of case-study cards, about and contact.
canonCard.viewport: Big name and one-line role, then a two-column grid of project cards.
